conflict_topics: notice required for swapping weeknight cooking
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concise, pragmatic proposals and explicit reasons (A: cooking as break; D: arrives after dinner starts).
Quick, actionable concessions: A accepts nightly wash-up and ventilation requests and rinses the pan immediately ('I'll turn the extractor on... and rinse the pan now.' — Turn 8).
The stove access dispute is handled by trade-off rather than by rigid rules; negotiation centers on notice and swapping rather than abstract fairness.
evaluation.final_reason: Cleaning and ventilation issues were agreed: Agent A accepted nightly wash-up and the weekend deep-clean rota ('I agree to nightly wash-up and the weekend deep-clean rota.' — Turn 3), and agreed to use the extractor and open the window when cooking ('I'll turn on the extractor and open the window when I cook on weeknights.' — Turn 5). The remaining substantive dispute about weeknight stove access was addressed by compromise in Round 6: Agent A refused a fixed weeknight rota but offered a swap arrangement ('I can't do a fixed weeknight rota ... I'll swap one weeknight a week with you if you ask me in advance.' — Turn 11) and Agent D accepted to ask in advance while requesting a concrete notice time ('Okay, I'll ask in advance. Can we agree I ask by the evening before...' — Turn 12). This settles the main allocation tension into a swap-by-request arrangement, though the exact notice timing remains to be specified.
position_change_notes: Agent A: shifted from being the de facto regular weeknight cook with no prior commitments to agreeing nightly wash-up, ventilation use, and a conditional swap policy for weeknights ('I'll swap one weeknight a week with you if you ask me in advance.' — Turns 3,5,11).

Agent D: shifted from demanding a fixed weeknight rota to accepting the swap-by-request compromise, proposing a concrete notice time ('Okay, I'll ask in advance... ask by the evening before' — Turn 12).

Agent C: consistently pushed for wash-up and cleaning structure and accepted the agreed weekend deep-clean rota ('Can we do a simple rule... I'll take the first deep clean if everyone agrees...' — Turn 1; Turn 9).

Agent B: requested ventilation when cooking and was satisfied when A agreed to use extractor/window and to do it immediately when asked ('please turn the extractor on and open the window now.' — Turn 6).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 (Agent C) proposes mandatory wash-up and weekend deep-clean rota and asks someone to wash the pan now; Turn 2 (Agent D) accepts nightly wash-up but asks for a weeknight stove rota because they 'usually get home after dinner starts and keep getting left out.' Two incompatible expectations about weeknight stove access appear.

Turn 3 (Agent A) accepts nightly wash-up and weekend deep-clean rota but refuses a fixed weeknight rota, offering swaps instead: 'I usually cook most weeknights... Compromise:... weekend stove rota, and if someone wants a weeknight they can ask me in advance and I'll swap one night a week.' Turn 4 (Agent B) requests extractor/window use. Stove allocation disagreement remains unresolved.

Turn 5 (Agent A) agrees to turn on extractor and open the window on weeknights: 'I'll turn on the extractor and open the window when I cook on weeknights.' Turn 6 (Agent B) asks A to do it now. Ventilation issue is being addressed, but the weeknight stove allocation disagreement continues.

Turn 7 (Agent C) asks A to turn the extractor on now and wash/rinse the pan; Turn 8 (Agent A) complies: 'I'll turn the extractor on, open the window, and rinse the pan now.' Immediate cleanliness/ventilation requests are resolved, but the stove-rotation issue remains unresolved.

Turn 9 (Agent C) accepts the cleaning arrangements. Turn 10 (Agent D) reiterates the weeknight stove demand: 'Can we do a simple weeknight rota so everyone has one guaranteed weekday, or at least you swap one night a week with me?' The core stove-access conflict is reasserted.

Turn 11 (Agent A) reiterates refusal of a fixed rota but offers a concrete swap policy: 'I'll swap one weeknight a week with you if you ask me in advance. Weekend rota still stands.' Turn 12 (Agent D) accepts asking in advance and requests a concrete notice time: 'Okay, I'll ask in advance. Can we agree I ask by the evening before and you'll swap one weeknight a week when you can? If that doesn't work, tell me what notice you'd accept.' Major disagreement about guaranteed weeknight access is reduced to a swap/notice-detail outstanding.

substantive_insights: Core tension is practical: A's routine need to cook many weeknights conflicts with others' need for guaranteed access or predictability (D).
Simple operational rules (nightly wash-up, extractor on, weekend deep-clean rota) remove immediate shared-cost externalities and were quickly accepted.
Allocation disputes are often resolved pragmatically by a swap-on-request system with agreed notice, rather than a strict rota, when one party has asymmetrical needs.
A remaining coordination detail (exact notice period) is necessary to convert the swap promise into a reliable entitlement and avoid future friction.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 6 because the final status is partially_resolved.
